I am an old man now, and this small piece of land I rent is all I have to feed my family. I will put down some chemical fertilizer—maybe half a bag—because the soil here is weak and maize will not grow tall without help, and I will also spread manure from my goats like I have always done. My sons and grandchildren will come to help me weed and plant, but I must pay two young men from the village to help with the heavy digging at the start since my back is not strong anymore. I will sow the seed I kept from last year's harvest, and I do not have money for sprays or pipes for water, so we wait for the rains.
